guard_streams.source: Latest telecoms and pay-TV complaints revealed - Q4 2025
guard_streams.write_limit: Quarterly complaint rates and reasons are service-quality context and cannot establish selected-parcel broadband availability, orderability or measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Q4 2025 complaints update on 11 May 2026.
The figures cover October to December 2025.
Overall complaints increased on the previous quarter for the first time since 2023.
Broadband complaints decreased.
Landline complaints decreased.
Pay-TV complaints remained unchanged.
Mobile complaints increased after mid-contract price-rise announcements.
TalkTalk and Vodafone generated the highest broadband complaint rates.
Plusnet and Virgin Media generated the lowest broadband complaint rates.
O2 generated the highest mobile complaint rate, mainly involving contract issues.

guard_streams.source: Broadband complaints fall to record low
guard_streams.write_limit: Complaint volumes and provider rankings are aggregate service-quality indicators and cannot verify selected-parcel network coverage or measured performance.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the record-low complaints update on 23 July 2026.
The figures cover January to March 2026.
Average broadband complaints fell to six per 100,000 subscribers.
The broadband complaint rate was the lowest since Ofcom began publishing the data in 2011.
The comparable 2011 peak was 40 complaints per 100,000 subscribers.
Combined telecoms and pay-TV complaints fell.
TalkTalk generated the highest broadband complaint rate.
Plusnet and Sky generated the lowest broadband complaint rates.
Sky Mobile generated the highest pay-monthly mobile complaint rate.
Ofcom publishes complaint figures to help consumers compare provider service quality.

guard_streams.source: Social tariffs: Cheaper broadband and phone packages
guard_streams.write_limit: Tariff eligibility, prices and advertised package speeds are affordability information and do not establish physical network availability or measured speed at a selected parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the social-tariff guide on 6 March 2024.
The guide was last updated on 22 June 2026.
Eligibility commonly depends on receipt of specified means-tested benefits.
Listed social-tariff prices generally range from £10 to £24 per month.
Most listed social tariffs offer advertised speeds above 30 Mbit/s.
Eligible customers can generally switch to a social tariff without charge.
Social tariffs generally do not have mid-contract price rises.
Customers can generally leave a social tariff without an early termination fee.
The guide lists social tariffs from multiple broadband and mobile providers.
Customers apply directly to the provider and may need an eligibility check.

guard_streams.source: Money saving tips for phone, broadband and pay-TV
guard_streams.write_limit: Money-saving guidance, contract advice and comparison options do not verify selected-parcel coverage, live orderability or measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the money-saving guide on 1 July 2026.
The guide directs eligible customers to social tariffs.
Phone and broadband contracts commonly have 12, 18 or 24-month minimum terms.
Providers must send end-of-contract notifications.
Customers are advised to shop around when a contract ends.
The guide recommends accredited comparison sites and provider checks.
Switching provider can reduce bills or improve package value.
Customers are advised to review whether bundled services remain useful.
Unused subscriptions or services can be paused or cancelled where permitted.
Customers may save by reducing allowances or choosing broadband-only service.

guard_streams.source: Comparing customer service: choosing the best home broadband, mobile and landline provider
guard_streams.write_limit: Provider satisfaction, complaints handling and call-centre metrics are aggregate service-quality evidence and cannot establish selected-parcel broadband service or speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the provider comparison page on 18 May 2023.
The page was last updated on 25 May 2026.
The linked Comparing Customer Service publication is the eighth report in the series.
The report principally covers customer-service performance during 2024.
It includes comparisons with 2022 and 2023 where available.
Ofcom describes the report as moving to a biennial publication cycle.
Overall satisfaction with communications services remained high.
Complaints-handling satisfaction improved in several measures.
Call abandonment and answer-time performance varied between providers.
Ofcom notes that an EE data resubmission may require some 2025-report figures to be restated.
